name: Ironclad Agrisystems Traverse Cultivator Rig
description:
The Traverse Cultivator Rig is a heavy-duty ground vehicle originally designed by Ironclad Agrisystems for use in GLMZ's reclaimed agricultural zones — the vast, semi-toxic growing fields in the city's outer ring where vertical and chemical farming operations require mobile platforms capable of traversing unstable, chemically saturated soil. The Traverse is built on a six-track chassis with variable-width stance: its track assemblies can splay outward to distribute load across a wider footprint for soft ground, or contract inward for navigating narrow passages. Each track is independently driven and steered, allowing the vehicle to pivot in place, crab sideways, and negotiate terrain that would immobilize conventional wheeled vehicles. The cab seats three and is fully sealed and filtered against agricultural chemical exposure, with a positive-pressure air system that maintains breathable atmosphere even in heavily contaminated environments.

The vehicle's operational versatility comes from its universal attachment interface — a heavy hydraulic coupling system at the front and rear that accepts a standardized range of Ironclad Agrisystems implements: tillage arrays, fungal inoculation sprayers, soil compaction analyzers, and cargo flatbeds among them. In its base configuration without implements, the Traverse is simply a capable, chemically-hardened terrain vehicle with significant cargo capacity in its rear bay. This modularity has made it attractive far beyond its intended agricultural context. The sealed cab, chemical resistance, and terrain capability make it a practical platform for operating in GLMZ's contaminated industrial zones, collapsed infrastructure districts, and the outer-ring Deadlands where conventional vehicles deteriorate rapidly.

Ironclad Agrisystems sells the Traverse openly to licensed agricultural operators and leases fleet units to contracted farming collectives. The vehicle's presence in non-agricultural contexts is common enough that it no longer attracts automatic suspicion — a Traverse moving through a contaminated district is assumed to be an agri-contractor until proven otherwise, a cover that various operators have learned to exploit.

specifications.drive_system: Six independent tracks, variable-width stance (2.1 m contracted, 3.4 m splayed)
specifications.attachment_points: Front and rear universal hydraulic coupling (Ironclad IAS-7 standard)
specifications.cab_protection: CBRN-rated positive pressure filtration, rated to Class IV agricultural chemical exposure
specifications.dimensions: 6.1 m length, variable width, 2.8 m height (cab)

tactical_use: In legitimate agricultural use, the Traverse moves equipment and materials across the unstable outer-ring growing fields. In gray-market use, it serves as a terrain-capable transport through contaminated zones that other vehicles cannot enter — the Deadlands, the collapsed Refinery District, and the chemically saturated former industrial areas of the outer ring. Its sealed cab allows personnel to transit these areas without exposure gear. For extraction or resupply operations in contaminated terrain, the Traverse is frequently the only practical option. Its agricultural appearance provides plausible cover in outer-ring districts where agri-contractor traffic is routine.
cultural_context: The Traverse is not glamorous. In GLMZ's vehicle culture, it occupies the same aesthetic space as a work truck — functional, ubiquitous in the outer ring, and almost entirely invisible to the kind of people who don't work the outer ring. This invisibility is its primary social asset. Runners and operators who work the contaminated outer districts have a deep, practical appreciation for the Traverse that inner-ring residents simply cannot share. There is a small but dedicated modification community that builds combat and utility packages onto Traverse rigs — armored cabs, weapon mounts on the implement couplings, sensor arrays — creating vehicles that look like agricultural equipment until they don't.
known_users: Runner teams operating in the Deadlands or Refinery District
Kael Ostro (outer-ring fixer, operates a heavily modified Traverse as a mobile operations base)
story_hooks: An Ironclad Agrisystems fleet Traverse has been reported overdue on a routine outer-ring cultivation run. When the player characters locate it, the cab is sealed, the engine is running, and the occupants are gone. The rear bay contains a cargo that doesn't appear in any manifest.

Someone has been using a Traverse to move something through the Refinery District at night. The outer-ring community knows better than to ask questions, but whatever is being moved is leaving behind traces that are alarming even for the Refinery District.

A modification specialist in the Verge Corridors is offering to build a combat package onto a player-owned or acquired Traverse — implement coupling weapon mounts, armored cab panels, sensor arrays — but they want payment in something other than currency.

Ironclad Agrisystems has discovered that a batch of Traverse units sold to a farming collective three years ago never actually reached the collective. The collective has no record of receiving them. Ironclad wants to know where twelve heavy terrain vehicles went, and the trail leads into the Deadlands.
related_entities: The Pipe Seams Hold (Until They Don't)

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutal, angular six-track utility vehicle with a utilitarian cab mounted high over a wide, splayed chassis. The design prioritizes function over aesthetics — exposed hydraulic lines, reinforced frame members, and a boxy operator's compartment dominate. The track assemblies are massive and heavily treaded, capable of dramatic stance adjustment that visibly changes the vehicle's footprint. First impression: industrial, purpose-built, intimidating.
physical_description.dimensions: 6.1 m length, 2.1–3.4 m width (variable), 2.8 m height. Vehicle-class; occupies significant space in any environment.
physical_description.weight_description: Heavy — approximately 8,500 kg dry weight. Requires dedicated parking and can sink into soft ground if stance is not properly adjusted. Mounted on its own weight-distribution system.
physical_description.primary_material: Welded steel frame with composite reinforcement panels. Tracks are elastomer-steel composite with tungsten carbide tooth inserts. Cab is structural steel with polycarbonate viewport strips.
physical_description.finish: Industrial matte — weathered gray-green outer paneling from factory primer + accumulated road chemical staining. Hydraulic lines are bare steel with zinc plating showing oxidation. Rubber track treads are heavily worn and discolored with soil and chemical residue.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primer gray-green base with worn institutional yellow striping (safety markings on track guards and cab edges). Ironclad logo (white serif type) stenciled on both sides of cab. Rust bloom visible at seam lines and fastener points.
physical_description.interface_elements: Operator cab interior visible through reinforced polycarbonate windows — analog pressure gauges, mechanical lever controls for track steering and stance adjustment, digital display panel mounted on dashboard showing hydraulic pressure and fuel status. External attachment couplings (front/rear) are massive ISO-standard quick-release hydraulic connectors with color-coded fluid lines (red, blue, yellow pressure circuits visible). Mounting points for implements are visibly worn from repeated coupling cycles.
distinctive_features: Six independently-articulated track assemblies with visible piston rods controlling stance width — in splayed position, chassis spreads to nearly 3.4 m, in contracted mode hunches inward
Dual hydraulic pump housings mounted on engine block, visible on side of vehicle
Heavy-duty front and rear towing/coupling frame extensions that accept IAS-7 standard implement connectors
Positive-pressure cab air intake manifold mounted on roof (intake filter visible)
Tool racks welded to exterior of cab — carbide digging tools, repair kits, spare track segments stored openly
Worn hydraulic line routing along the frame; several lines show patched sections wrapped in pressure tape
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: IRONCLAD AGRISYSTEMS stenciled in white on both sides of cab. Model designation TRAVERSE CULTIVATOR RIG in smaller font below. Regulatory placards (CBRN CLASS IV certification, fuel type, pressure ratings) mounted on cab rear. Serial number stamped into chassis frame. Fleet operators often add their own paint-spray codes on track guards.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-used. Exterior shows chemical staining (rust spots, discoloration where crop-treatment residue has etched the paint). Track treads are visibly compressed and worn; tread pattern is still aggressive but clearly not new. Hydraulic lines may show minor seeping at coupling points (normal wear). Cab interior is industrial and spartan — no comfort features, heavily stained by operator sweat and soil. The vehicle operates but shows honest wear from frequent deployment in harsh environments.
